audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers carried the chart Skill/Akali/Akali/Skill/Skill/Akali/Akali, which contradicts the packet chart AND the whys sitting directly beside it. whys[0] says 'You own level 1' under a 'Skill' token; whys[1] says 'coinflip at 2' under 'Akali'; whys[2] says 'skill-dependent' under 'Akali'; whys[3] says 'She pulls ahead' under 'Skill'; whys[4] calls level 6 'her hardest window' under 'Skill'; whys[6] describes Nautilus catching her for his team under 'Akali'. Also diff read 'EVEN' while diffRating is 8.5/10 and report[14] calls it a hard matchup.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Nautilus/Skill/Skill/Akali/Akali/Akali/Nautilus, which matches every why verbatim. The prose was right and the tokens were wrong on five of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Akali, Akali, Akali, Nautilus in BOTH layers as matched pairs, ratings realigned, and diff changed EVEN -> HARD to agree with the 8.5/10 difficulty.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-3 spike and the early block both claimed Akali 'has no Shroud yet' at level 3, and the level-6 spike gave Perfect Execution no cooldown.
audit.why: Akali has all three basics by level 3 in most orders — asserting Twilight Shroud is unavailable there is a claim the kit does not support and would get a player killed. The real level-3 advantage is her energy pool: Five Point Strike costs 110 energy at rank 1, so she cannot trade poke-for-poke against a shield.
audit.corrected: Level-3 spike and early block rebuilt on the 110-energy Q cost. Perfect Execution's 120/90/60 cooldown and Twilight Shroud's 20s rank-1 cooldown now anchor the level-4-6 advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Shroud charges' was asserted twice; the untargetability was described only against 'hook', ignoring that Depth Charge is also a targeted spell; wants.you[2] told the player to knock her up 'mid-execute'; wants.you[1] wrote 'her shuriman E' instead of Shuriken Flip.
audit.why: Riot's Twilight Shroud text is a single cast with move speed and untargetability — no charges appear anywhere in the kit file. 'Unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks' applies to BOTH Dredge Line and Depth Charge, which is the single decisive interaction of this matchup and was half-stated. Whether Depth Charge can be landed on a champion mid-dash is not in the kit text, so the timing instruction was replaced with the verifiable one: hit her when she lands.
audit.corrected: Shroud restated as a 20s cooldown that voids Q and R alike; charges claim removed; Perfect Execution and Shuriken Flip named; R advice retimed to the landing, not the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named no numbers and referred to 'your committal tool' generically.
audit.why: The two windows that decide the lane are Twilight Shroud at 20s rank 1 and Perfect Execution at 60s once ranked up.

edits.before: You'd own this with Q-into-root and W burn, but her first Shroud charge can already dodge your Q wind-up, so it's skill-dependent.
edits.after: You'd own this with Q-into-root and W burn, but Twilight Shroud drops before the anchor lands and voids it, so it's skill-dependent.

edits.before: She pulls ahead: Twilight Shroud reliably eats your Q pin and her E-dash poke chips you down between your cooldowns.
edits.after: She pulls ahead: Twilight Shroud eats your Q pin every 20s and Shuriken Flip chips you down between your cooldowns.

edits.before: Her R two-part dash plus execute all-ins you the moment your W shield drops and Q is on cooldown — her hardest window.
edits.after: Perfect Execution's two dashes and execute all-in you the moment Titan's Wrath drops and Q is down — her hardest window.

edits.before: Q-pull into passive-root plus Titan's Wrath splash burn lets you chunk her before she has Shroud or her E shuriken to disengage.
edits.after: Q-pull into passive-root plus Titan's Wrath splash burn chunks her while Five Point Strike still costs her 110 energy a cast.

edits.before: Force short trades at level 2-3 while Titan's Wrath is up and her shuriman E is her only escape
edits.after: Force short trades at level 2-3 while Titan's Wrath is up and Shuriken Flip is her only escape

edits.before: Bank your R for when she commits her two-part R dash, then knock her up mid-execute
edits.after: Bank your R for the instant she lands out of Perfect Execution, not while she is dashing

edits.before: At level 1 you're roughly even — no W or E yet, but a clean Q-pull into your passive root sets up a free auto trade she can't answer without burning E. Your real window is level 3: with Titan's Wrath splash-burn and your Q-pull-into-root combo online, every short trade is yours because she has no Shroud yet and her energy pool can't out-poke your shield. Bait her E shuriken, then land Q — if the anchor connects she's pinned and you win the exchange flat.
edits.after: At level 1 you own the exchange — Staggering Blow roots on your first attack and she has neither Twilight Shroud nor Shuriken Flip to answer it. Your real window is level 3: with Titan's Wrath splash-burn and your Q-pull-into-root combo online, every short trade is yours, because Five Point Strike costs 110 energy at rank 1 and she cannot spam it into your shield. Bait Shuriken Flip, then land Q — if the anchor connects she's pinned and you win the exchange flat.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 the lane starts slipping: she gets Shroud charges and learns to drop it the moment you wind up Q, so your only pin whiffs into an untargetable target. At 6 it gets worse — her R two-part dash plus execute lets her all-in the second your W shield drops and your Q is down. Hold your own R as the answer: don't waste it engaging, save it to knock her up while she's mid-R-dash, because that's the one moment her slipperiness can't save her.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 the lane starts slipping: Twilight Shroud is back every 20 seconds and she drops it the moment you wind up Q, so your only pin whiffs into a target your spells cannot select. At 6 it gets worse — Perfect Execution's two dashes and execute let her all-in the second Titan's Wrath drops and your Q is down. Hold your own R as the answer: don't waste it engaging, save it for the instant she lands out of a dash, because that's the one moment her slipperiness can't save her.

edits.before: - Akali Twilight Shroud: matchup-defining — Untargetable inside — hook needs a target. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Akali Twilight Shroud: 20s at rank 1 — untargetable inside, so Dredge Line and Depth Charge both need her outside it. - Perfect Execution: 60s once maxed. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Untargetable inside — hook needs a target. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Untargetable inside — your Q and R both need a target. It is down 20s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Akali's Twilight Shroud: Untargetable inside — hook needs a target. When it is down — Q-E + R her.
edits.after: Track Twilight Shroud: untargetable inside, so Q and R both need her out of it. When down — Q-E + R her.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged wants.foe[0] 'Drop Twilight Shroud' as a probable wrong name — that is a FALSE POSITIVE, Twilight Shroud is the correct name for Akali's W and the field was left alone. Two claims I could not verify and therefore did not write: whether Depth Charge can connect on Akali while she is mid-dash during Perfect Execution, and whether Shuriken Flip marking her own Twilight Shroud (Riot's text says 'first enemy or smoke cloud hit is marked') gives her a re-entry dash from outside the shroud — the second is a real, unmentioned interaction that a Nautilus player would want to know about, but the kit text does not confirm the range implication. Sample is only 24 games at 37.5%.
